chunks: Sama'ah asked him about a man who comes to the mosque when its people have already prayed: should he begin with the obligatory prayer or offer a voluntary prayer? So he said:

"If it is within a favorable time, then there is no harm in offering a voluntary prayer before the obligatory prayer. But if he fears the time will expire, he should delay it and begin with the obligatory prayer, for it is the right of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Then let him offer whatever voluntary prayer he wishes."

key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةِ: the mandatory prayer that must be prioritized when time is short
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque where the worshipper arrives
key_terms.الْوَقْتِ: the appointed time of the prayer
key_terms.حَقُّ اللَّهِ: the due right of Allah that takes precedence

ai.seo_question: If someone enters the mosque after the congregation has finished, should he pray a voluntary prayer first or the obligatory salat?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for someone who enters the mosque after the congregational salat has already been performed. If sufficient time remains, he may perform a voluntary prayer before the obligatory one; but if the prayer time is close to ending, he must begin with the obligatory salat, since it takes priority as the right of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
